Simulate a Fermi estimate

bf_fermi_simulate.Rd

Simulate a Fermi estimate

Usage

bf_fermi_simulate(
  components,
  fun,
  n_draws = 10000,
  use = c("posterior", "prior"),
  nonfinite = c("error", "drop")
)

Arguments

components

A named list of bf_prior and/or bf_posterior objects, sampled independently, or a numeric data frame with one joint draw per row. Joint draws are used in the supplied order, preserving dependence.

fun

A vectorised function whose arguments correspond to names(components). It must return one numeric value per input row.

n_draws

Number of Monte Carlo draws. For a data frame, this defaults to its number of rows and must match it if supplied.

use

For lists, "posterior" (default) uses posterior parameters when available. "prior" uses the priors attached to any posterior objects.

nonfinite

"error" (default) rejects non-finite inputs or outputs. "drop" excludes affected rows from both inputs and output.

Value

A bf_fermi object with draws, their corresponding inputs, the supplied fun, and n_dropped (the number of excluded rows).

Examples

joint <- data.frame(demand = c(100, 200, 300), capacity = c(80, 150, 250))
bf_fermi_simulate(joint, function(demand, capacity) demand - capacity)
#> $draws
#> [1] 20 50 50
#> 
#> $inputs
#>   demand capacity
#> 1    100       80
#> 2    200      150
#> 3    300      250
#> 
#> $fun
#> function (demand, capacity) 
#> demand - capacity
#> <environment: 0x6428422c9318>
#> 
#> $n_dropped
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "bf_fermi"
